title: fix: WP11_QUIRK_SHORT_APDU and WP11_QUIRK_NO_PSS defined but never applied
description:
wp11_token_db.h defines two quirk flags:
  WP11_QUIRK_NO_PSS  (0x01): RSA-PSS should be done client-side, not on-token
  WP11_QUIRK_SHORT_APDU (0x02): token only supports max 255-byte APDU body

Both flags appear in the token descriptor table but all entries have WP11_QUIRK_NONE. More critically, the PIV protocol code (wp11_proto_piv.c) does not check these flags anywhere — they are inert dead code.

Real-world impact:
- Some NitroKey and Feitian tokens do not support extended APDUs (>255 bytes). Sending a 256-byte RSA signature APDU to such a token will return 6700 (wrong length) or be silently truncated by the CCID layer.
- Some tokens do not implement RSA-PSS natively and need the padding done by the host.

Fix:
1. Wire WP11_QUIRK_SHORT_APDU into wp11_piv_sign and wp11_piv_ecdh: if quirk is set, split any APDU body >255 bytes using command chaining (CLA=0x10 for all but last, CLA=0x00 for last) per ISO 7816-4 §5.1.1.
2. Wire WP11_QUIRK_NO_PSS into the PKCS#11 signing path: if quirk is set and mechanism is CKM_RSA_PKCS_PSS, apply PSS padding in wolfCrypt and send raw CKM_RSA_X_509 to the token.
3. Assign correct quirks to known tokens in the database: research which NitroKey/Feitian models need WP11_QUIRK_SHORT_APDU.
4. Add a comment at each quirk check site explaining what real-world token behavior triggered the flag.
